uncited: For structural extensions, it solves dynamic appearance and geometry reconstruction by maintaining a canonical 3D Gaussian field and applying differentiable deformation to map primitives to target poses, distinguished by its focus on geometric articulation rather than semantic feature accumulation.
All methods in this family rely on the differentiable alpha-blending accumulation of feature vectors or colors during the rasterization step.
*   $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the vector (feature $\mathbf{f}_i$ or color $\mathbf{c}_i$) of the $i$-th Gaussian.
*   $\alpha_i$ is the opacity of the $i$-th Gaussian.
*   $\prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)$ is the transmittance from all preceding Gaussians $j < i$.
For structural extensions, all methods share a canonical space representation where 3D Gaussians are initialized in a reference pose (e.g., T-pose or neutral expression).
Deformation is achieved by mapping these canonical Gaussians to a target pose defined by parameters (e.g., skeleton joints, expression coefficients).
The rendering pipeline remains differentiable, allowing optimization of Gaussian attributes and deformation parameters via photometric loss.

GVA [222] proposes a surface-guided Gaussians re-initialization strategy to make the trained Gaussians better fit the input monocular video, addressing the unbalanced aggregation of Gaussians caused by densification and splitting operations.
The semantic extension family leverages the differentiable nature of 3D Gaussian Splatting to support open-vocabulary queries, a capability not natively present in standard color-based rendering.

The claim states that the 'structural extension family' addresses limitations of static 3DGS in modeling dynamic humans by building on techniques introduced for dynamic head reconstruction [S1]. However, the provided evidence from [S1] discusses methods for human body modeling (GVA, HAHA) and separate methods for head modeling (MonoGaussianAvatar, PSAvatar, GaussianHead). The evidence does not mention a 'structural extension family' nor does it explicitly state that the human body methods build upon the head reconstruction techniques. In fact, the text presents them as distinct areas or parallel advancements. Therefore, the specific causal link and terminology in the claim are not supported by the text.
